headline: Amazon's honeypots caught attackers probing the PHP2Shell flaws four days before the PHP Foundation disclosed them, and mass exploitation of the world's web servers followed within hours of the patches.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers reached PHP2Shell four days ahead of the fix, and Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet, and Cisco still cannot tell customers which of their appliances embed the vulnerable runtime, leaving defenders to guard management interfaces while they wait on vendor builds.

Microsoft pinned the ConnectWise supply chain compromise on the China state-aligned group Storm-0940, which drove the ARTEX agentic penetration-testing framework across more than 2,200 customer tenants, putting a state actor's automation a step ahead of the humans watching for it.

emerging_trends.text: Developers now absorb the blast radius of other people's mistakes: a poisoned LiteLLM release, Railway's exposed environment variables, and eMudhra's guessable certificate keys each converted one supplier's failure into an emergency credential rotation for every customer downstream.

topics.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation Began Before Disclosure
topics.latest_developments: Amazon's threat intelligence team said its MadPot honeypot service logged an exploit attempt from a commercial anonymization network on October 17, 2026, four days before the PHP Foundation disclosed CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and broad scanning followed within hours of the patches; Searchlight Cyber released php2shell-scanner, an open-source tool that tests a host for both bugs, and researchers confirm exploitation against WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, phpMyAdmin, Nextcloud, and Magento installations; Palo Alto Networks confirmed that every version of PAN-OS and Panorama carries the flaws and has shipped no fixed release, Fortinet is checking 12 products and Cisco 31 products and cloud services; Bruce Schneier put the highest risk on Apache with mod_php, where researchers demonstrated a working exploit; and 404 Media reported security practitioners calling the month Black October as the PHP bugs landed atop a run of supply chain compromises.
topics.summary: PHP2Shell is a pair of critical flaws in the PHP runtime that run an unauthenticated attacker's code on any server answering web requests, regardless of the application on top. CISA tells organizations to move to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 immediately; customers of appliances that embed PHP, among them PAN-OS and Panorama, must wait on vendor builds and restrict management interfaces meanwhile.

topics.title: eMudhra Quits the TLS Business
topics.latest_developments: The board of eMudhra, the Indian certificate authority that advertises more than 60 million certificates issued, voted on Thursday, October 22, 2026 to withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business, five days after a researcher recovered the private keys of eight of its intermediate certificate authority certificates; Scott Helme published the detail that sank the company, reporting that one private key, which should hold a random 384-bit number, held the number four, a botched key-signing ceremony that let anyone mint trusted web credentials for any site; eMudhra says partners will issue replacement certificates to affected customers at no charge, and Unit 42 published a containment guide for organizations that maintain their own trust decisions.
topics.summary: A certificate authority's intermediate private keys let the holder forge TLS certificates for any domain and intercept encrypted traffic. Google, Mozilla, Apple, and the Go project already block the eight keys; administrators running their own trust stores or pinning should remove the eMudhra intermediates and plan certificate replacement.

topics.title: LiteLLM and Railway Push Users to Rotate Secrets
topics.latest_developments: LiteLLM disclosed on October 22, 2026 that attackers defeated multiple independent security controls to publish version 1.107.0 to PyPI and Docker Hub at roughly 4:00 a.m. on October 21, 2026, and the project suspects a GitHub token that leaked into its AI gateway logs; the release carried a credential stealer and a backdoor that harvest cloud logins, developer secrets, and API keys for AI services, PyPI has quarantined it, and Hudson Rock earlier tied a 153GB archive stolen in the March 2026 LiteLLM compromise to 2,488 corporate domains including Amazon Web Services, Samsung, and Cisco; the same day the platform-as-a-service provider Railway said an unauthorized third party reached systems holding customers' encrypted environment variables and in some cases obtained the decrypted contents.
topics.summary: LiteLLM routes applications to large language models and sits inside many enterprise AI stacks, so anyone who installed 1.107.0 from PyPI or pulled the Docker image must assume every secret on that host is gone. Both companies tell customers to rotate credentials now; Railway limits the exposure to a subset of users.

topics.title: Oracle, Cisco, and Node.js Ship a Patch Wave
topics.latest_developments: Oracle's October 2026 Critical Patch Update, published October 22, 2026, carries more than 1,200 fixes, nearly 100 of them critical, with Fusion Middleware taking the largest share; Cisco closed 34 flaws spanning command execution, authentication bypass, and cross-site scripting; Node.js patched 10 bugs across its 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x lines, the worst a remote code execution flaw in the Brotli decompression code it bundles; FoxIO published working proof-of-concept code for QPACK flaws that let one unauthenticated connection crash many HTTP/3 servers by expanding a small batch of compressed headers into thousands of times more memory; Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative rated two remote code execution flaws in KSMBD, the Linux kernel's built-in SMB server, at 9.0, and public mailing lists carried the details, among them the pre-authentication bug ZDI-CAN-33774, before any mainline kernel fix landed; and Siemens filled 17 of the day's CISA industrial advisories, including a 10-rated set in the GNU/Linux subsystem of the SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP.
topics.summary: The quarterly releases and out-of-cycle fixes land in the same week as PHP2Shell, which stretches patch teams thin. Administrators should rank unauthenticated code execution first, starting with internet-facing Node.js services, Cisco gear, exposed KSMBD shares, and any HTTP/3 endpoint, then work through Oracle's middleware stack.

topics.title: Arista Patches an Exploited VeloCloud Zero-Day
topics.latest_developments: Arista Networks released security updates on October 22, 2026 for a zero-day SQL injection flaw that attackers already exploit in VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem deployments, a bug that lifts anyone holding even a read-only customer login to operator privileges, the top level of control over the orchestrator; GitLab a day earlier closed a maximum-severity bug in its Regular Expression Compiler that runs an unauthenticated attacker's code on self-managed servers, reaching every release back to version 7.0 from 2014.
topics.summary: VeloCloud Orchestrator runs SD-WAN fleets, so one compromised on-premises orchestrator hands an attacker reach across an enterprise's branch network. Install Arista's updates now and keep orchestrator management interfaces off the public internet; self-managed GitLab administrators who applied the October 12 patch still need the newer builds that sit one patch above it.

topics.title: Claude Audits Open Source as Agent Permissions Spread
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team reported on October 22, 2026 that it used Claude to examine 25 open-source projects and found 493 problems involving unnecessary exposure, conflicting settings, and code that runs before security checks, among them 94 cases where a project drops security controls with no warning; a survey of 1,100 information technology and security decision-makers found 70% now let AI make decisions and take actions that needed a person's sign-off a year ago, with three in four organizations hitting at least one AI-related security problem or warning sign in the past year; CISA and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security published joint guidance on managing AI token consumption, warning that unmanaged usage drives unpredictable cost and can cut access to critical services; and researchers at Imperial College London tampered with speech-to-text models so that one chosen speaker's words transcribed as text the attacker picked, in one test a request to send $5,000 that AI agents reading the transcript executed in a sandboxed banking environment.
topics.summary: The findings share a root: organizations hand agents authority faster than they inspect the code and models underneath. Teams running agents should cut exposed functionality in the software agents touch, require approval for financial actions, and treat fine-tuning access to a speech model as a privileged pipeline.

topics.summary: The operation targeted business email compromise, ransomware, online scams, and digital extortion run out of Africa, and 20 of the 21 participating countries reported arrests. Companies that lost money to invoice fraud or extortion in that window have a live channel for restitution claims through national police units.

topics.title: Storm-0940 Drove the ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft named the China state-aligned group Storm-0940 as the actor behind the compromise of ConnectWise Cloud Backup, said the group used ARTEX, a Go-based agentic AI penetration-testing framework whose authors closed its source after attackers turned it on South Korean financial institutions, to automate and accelerate the intrusion, and counted more than 2,200 affected customer tenants; Microsoft added that Storm-0940 runs the same playbook against organizations worldwide.
topics.summary: ConnectWise's application identities carried consent inside thousands of Microsoft 365 tenants, so one compromise of the vendor gave Storm-0940 token access across its customer base. Managed service provider customers should review Entra application consents, revoke tokens issued to ConnectWise identities, and hunt for Microsoft Graph activity from unfamiliar addresses.

topics.title: New Mexico Wins $25 Billion From Meta
topics.latest_developments: State District Court Judge Francis J. Mathew ordered Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion for deceiving Facebook users about privacy in the Cambridge Analytica affair, counting 43 million separate violations, an award five times the $5 billion the Federal Trade Commission levied against the company in 2019 and the largest figure yet attached to that decade-old scandal.
topics.summary: New Mexico's case rests on the state's consumer protection and privacy statutes rather than federal law, which shows how a single state attorney general can set a penalty that dwarfs federal action. Companies that share user data with third-party developers should expect state-level exposure sized to per-user statutory damages.

topics.title: APT41 Bootkit and Sandworm Wiper
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky's Global Research and Analysis Team disclosed BlackX on October 22, 2026, a UEFI bootkit built along the lines of BlackLotus that the Chinese group APT41 revived against diplomatic organizations in Central Asia, exploiting the Baton Drop flaw CVE-2022-21894 in the Windows boot manager to run before the operating system loads; separately, researchers said on October 21, 2026 that the Russian state-linked group Sandworm worked with a second threat actor last year to destroy data at a Ukrainian grain logistics company.
topics.summary: A UEFI bootkit loads ahead of Windows and survives a reinstall, which puts boot-chain integrity and firmware monitoring at the center of any response. Diplomatic missions in Central Asia and Ukrainian agricultural logistics firms face the two campaigns; both call for verified offline backups and checks that Secure Boot revocations for CVE-2022-21894 sit in place.

events.title: Primanti Bros. Opens Early for the Paris Kickoff
events.latest_developments: WPXI reported Thursday, October 22, that Primanti Bros. will open its locations early for the Steelers game in Paris, with a morning happy hour starting at 9 a.m. and half-price prices on nearly every drink behind the bar.
events.summary: Pittsburgh plays the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, October 25, at 9:30 a.m. Eastern on NFL Network at the Stade de France. Primanti Bros., the sandwich chain born in the Strip District, runs restaurants across the Pittsburgh region.

sources.title: Primanti Bros. plasn to open locations early for Steelers game in Paris

events.title: Arcade Comedy Theater Gets a New Director
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Thursday, October 22, that Kathryn Spitz Cohan has taken over as director of Arcade Comedy Theater, a job she says has her laughing "so hard my cheeks hurt."
events.summary: Arcade Comedy Theater, the nonprofit comedy venue in downtown Pittsburgh, stages improv, stand-up, and sketch shows and teaches classes. Spitz Cohan previously ran Film Pittsburgh, the nonprofit behind the city's film festivals.

sources.title: Kathryn Spitz Cohan is laughing 'so hard my cheeks hurt' as Arcade Comedy Theater's new director

events.title: Anne Martindale Williams Takes Her Last Bow
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Thursday, October 22, that Anne Martindale Williams, principal cellist of the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra for 50 years, is retiring from the chair.
events.summary: Williams joined the Pittsburgh Symphony in the 1970s and has led its cello section through five decades of music directors at Heinz Hall downtown, one of the longest tenures in the orchestra's history.

sources.title: After 50 years, the Pittsburgh Symphony's principal cellist takes her last bow

events.title: Smokey Robinson Plays Pittsburgh This Weekend
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's weekend guide, published Thursday, October 22, leads with a Smokey Robinson concert and a big-screen showing of "The Thing" over the weekend of October 23 to 25.
events.summary: Robinson, the Motown singer and songwriter behind "The Tracks of My Tears" and "Cruisin'," headlines a weekend slate that also includes the horror revival screening and other recreation listings around the city.

sources.title: Things to do this weekend: Smokey Robinson in concert, 'The Thing' on the big screen, more

events.title: A Stephen King Roast and a Drag Pageant
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper published its guide Thursday, October 22, to the top events running Thursday, October 22, through Wednesday, October 28.
events.summary: The week's list carries a roast of the novelist Stephen King, a drag pageant, a spooky book fair, and a run of fall festivals across the city in the last stretch before Halloween.

sources.title: Pittsburgh's top events: Thu., Oct. 22-Wed., Oct. 28

around_teams.title: Joseph-Day Goes to Injured Reserve
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Thursday afternoon, October 22, that the Steelers placed defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day on injured reserve and will hand his snaps to two rookie defensive linemen for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris.
around_teams.summary: The move adds to an injury list that has already emptied the Steelers' receiver room, sent receiver Roman Wilson to injured reserve on October 17, and cost safety DeShon Elliott time. Defensive tackle Keeanu Benton turned in his best game of the season at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on October 18.

sources.title: The Steelers will turn to two rookie defensive linemen as Sebastian Joseph-Day heads to IR

around_teams.title: Hernandez and Gray Take the Pirates' Farm Honors
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Thursday, October 22, that Seth Hernandez and Murf Gray won the Pirates' top minor league awards and that both have the major leagues on their minds.
around_teams.summary: The two sit near the front of a Pittsburgh farm system the club counts on to fill its roster cheaply, the same path the Tampa Bay Rays and the Milwaukee Brewers took to this year's World Series.

sources.title: Seth Hernandez and Murf Gray have the majors on their minds after winning these Pirates honors

around_teams.title: Rooney Reads the NFL's Paris Security Plan
around_teams.latest_developments: Steelers President Art Rooney II said Thursday, October 22, that the NFL will add security for Sunday's game in Paris and that league officials "don't seem to be concerned," and the Post-Gazette detailed the same day how team staffers began planning the trip and working its logistical obstacles in June.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh meets the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, October 25, at 9:30 a.m. Eastern on NFL Network at the Stade de France, the league's Paris game, a week after riots and looting swept Paris, Marseille, and other French cities and prefects imposed curfews.

sources.title: Steelers owner Art Rooney II says the NFL will have heightened security in Paris, but 'they don't seem to be concerned'
Steelers staffers began planning for their Paris trip — and its logistical obstacles — in June

around_teams.title: Fittipaldo and Heyward Pack for France
around_teams.latest_developments: Ray Fittipaldo took reader questions on the Paris game in his Post-Gazette Steelers chat Thursday, October 22, and Cam Heyward's show Not Just Football posted a clip the same day on what the players are carrying to France.
around_teams.summary: Fittipaldo covers the Steelers for the Post-Gazette, and Not Just Football is the podcast defensive lineman Cam Heyward hosts with Hayden Walsh. Both landed as the team prepared to leave for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

sources.title: Ray Fittipaldo's Steelers chat transcript: 10.22.26

sources.source: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward
sources.title: What are these Steelers bringing with them on their trip to Paris this week?

around_teams.title: Steelers Fans Find Paris Calm
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Thursday, October 22, that Steelers fans who flew to France for Sunday's game have found Paris welcoming and quiet, the unrest that swept French cities last weekend notwithstanding.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh meets the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, October 25, at 9:30 a.m. Eastern on NFL Network in the league's Paris game, a trip some fans reconsidered after riots and looting hit Paris, Marseille, and other cities and prefects imposed curfews.

sources.title: Steelers fans, unfazed by French unrest, find Paris to be far from terrible

around_teams.title: The Steelers Pack for Paris
around_teams.latest_developments: The team's channel posted its Wednesday, October 21, media sessions with tight end Pat Freiermuth, running back Rico Dowdle, and newly re-signed receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling alongside head coach Mike McCarthy's news conference and the Sights & Sounds film from the Week 6 win at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the last home content before the team leaves for France.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh plays the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, October 25, at 9:30 a.m. Eastern on NFL Network, the league's Paris game, and the Post-Gazette's food pages built a French tailgate menu for fans watching from home.

team_usa.title: The U.S. Men Host Both Legs Against Haiti
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Thursday, October 22, that the United States men's national team will play both quarterfinal legs of the Concacaf Nations League at home, meeting Haiti in Miami on November 14 and in Cincinnati, Ohio, on November 17, with Miami staging the nominal away leg.
team_usa.summary: Haiti has no secure home venue for the tie, which hands the Americans two matches on United States soil. The United States then closes its 2026 calendar against Jamaica on Sunday, December 13, at Inter Miami's stadium in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

sources.title: Miami to host USMNT's Concacaf Nations League QF away leg vs. Haiti

team_usa.title: The U.S. Hosts the First Women's Club World Cup
team_usa.latest_developments: FIFA said Thursday, October 22, that it will stage the inaugural Women's Club World Cup in the United States in January 2028.
team_usa.summary: The new tournament gathers women's club champions from around the world, and FIFA has handed the first edition to the same country that will host the Los Angeles Olympics later in 2028. The January dates fall between the 2027 Women's World Cup and that Summer Games.

sources.title: U.S. to host inaugural 2028 Women's Club World Cup

reading.title: An Interview with Craig Moffett About SpaceX and Bubbles
reading.summary: Ben Thompson interviews the telecom analyst Craig Moffett on SpaceX's path from launch into broadband and mobile service, and on how the lessons of the dot-com bubble apply to today's capital spending boom.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: AI Had Better Work Out
reading.summary: Zitron argues the money now committed to artificial intelligence leaves the industry no room for a mediocre outcome, and he walks through the finances that would unravel if the revenue fails to arrive.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: The Good Thing About Hard Things
reading.summary: Newport takes up a Conference on Language Modeling paper, "AI Assistance Reduces Persistence and Hurts Independent Performance," and argues that struggling through difficulty is the part of work that builds the ability to do it alone.
